cases.sourceText: Scientific documents combine continuous prose with equations, tables, references, and technical terminology. A useful reading assistant should translate the prose while preserving the original meaning and the structure of the document. Researchers often read the same paragraph several times to understand an unfamiliar method and compare it with earlier work. Local language models can support this process without sending the document to a remote service. Their practical speed depends on memory bandwidth, processor instructions, worker threads, and the amount of context being processed. A short answer may finish before the processor reaches a steady operating state, so repeated measurements with longer outputs are useful. Prompt processing and token generation should be measured separately because they perform different kinds of computation. A fair comparison also records the exact model file, inference settings, and device conditions. The goal of this experiment is to produce a faithful Chinese translation and retain enough timing information to distinguish engine performance from application overhead.
